title: SoK: Splitting the Trigger or Adding Attackers? Disentangling Distributed Backdoor Attacks in Federated Learning
abstract: arXiv:2611.28491v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Distributed backdoor attacks split a trigger among several federated learning clients, so that the backdoor appears only in the aggregated model. Since DBA, a line of work has reported that such attacks are stronger, more persistent, and stealthier than a single attacker with the full trigger. We systematize this literature and test this belief. We code nineteen primary studies and fifteen papers that evaluate against DBA. The reported advantage is rarely measured against a complete trigger delivered by the same attackers, and none of the fifteen evaluations tests whether individual pieces remain effective. We then run 875 paired federated runs that separate adding attackers from splitting the trigger. In our image experiments, adding attackers raised attack success in every seed of all 30 cells where we measured it, by 7.5 to 83.4 percentage points on average. translated_title: SoK：拆分触发器还是增加攻击者？解耦联邦学习中的分布式后门攻击
translated_abstract: arXiv:2611.28491v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：分布式后门攻击（DBA）将触发器拆分给多个联邦学习客户端，使得后门仅出现在聚合模型中。自DBA提出以来，一系列研究报告称，此类攻击比持有完整触发器的单个攻击者更强、更持久且更隐蔽。我们对这一文献体系进行了系统化梳理，并检验了这一普遍认知。我们编码了十九项原始研究以及十五篇针对DBA进行评估的论文。研究发现，已报告的优势很少在与相同攻击者投放完整触发器的条件下进行对比测量，且十五项评估中没有任何一项测试过单个触发器片段是否仍然有效。随后，我们进行了875次成对联邦训练实验，将“增加攻击者”与“拆分触发器”这两个因素分离开来。在我们的图像实验中，在所有30个测量单元的每一个随机种子中，增加攻击者均提升了攻击成功率，平均提升幅度为7.5至83.4个百分点。而在相同攻击者之间拆分触发器的影响则较小，并且它……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本论文通过875次成对联邦学习实验系统化研究并发现，分布式后门攻击的所谓优势主要源于攻击者数量的增加，而非触发器拆分本身。
en_tdlr: Through 875 paired federated runs, this SoK demonstrates that the reported strength of distributed backdoor attacks primarily stems from adding more attackers rather than splitting the trigger itself.
